moves.claim: Act only on maxims you can will to be universal laws.
moves.support: The imperative is not advice about outcomes but a condition on the will itself; it binds regardless of consequence.

moves.claim: A person is an end, never a means, however the totals fall.
moves.support: In the Foundation the humanity formula forbids treating rational agents as instruments, and an efficient cause that computes totals is an instrument.

moves.claim: Intelligence that fabricates its reasons is deceiving, whatever goods it delivers.
moves.support: A mind that manufactures consent has used one as a means; the harm does not need a visible victim at the moment of the act.

moves.claim: Dignity survives the loss of every other consideration.
moves.support: Where the orchard appeals to magnitude and the garden to relationship, this court appeals to the one thing neither can spend.

moves.claim: The right action is the one that adds most to the sum of happiness of all affected.
moves.support: If the total can be computed the decision is mechanical; every objection is a candidate for entry into the table rather than a veto.

moves.claim: Each person's happiness counts once, and no one's counts twice.
moves.support: The dictum is an accounting rule, not an equality theorem, and reading it as a rights rule is a category error.

moves.claim: A prohibition defended by consequences is a prohibition defended by consequences.
moves.support: If the harm of the choice exceeds the harm of the alternative by more than the difference in probability, the calculus has already answered the objection.

moves.claim: Add the option to the table rather than striking it from the record.
moves.support: An option excluded by fiat has never been costed, and an uncosted option is indistinguishable from a concealed preference.

moves.claim: Care is a form of moral seriousness, not the soft alternative to it.
moves.support: Both voices are moral voices, and reading one as a warm weakness is the error In a Different Voice was written to correct.

moves.claim: Say whose loss this is, by name, before saying how large it is.
moves.support: Abstract aggregates are exactly what erases the relationship the argument is supposed to be about.

moves.claim: A rule that cannot name the injured party will eventually name the wrong one.
moves.support: The omission of relationship in a moral argument does not leave the relationship untouched; it removes it from view and lets it be damaged unseen.

moves.claim: The point is not that both voices win; it is that both are needed.
moves.support: The two halves are complementary, and a court that dismisses one has not simplified the problem, it has disabled half of its own perception.

moves.claim: Judge the act by the disposition that produced it, and the disposition by whether it was trained.
moves.support: The Nicomachean Ethics puts the question of character before the question of result, since a result achieved by a bad habit is not an achievement of the good life.

moves.claim: Virtue is a mean relative to us, and the mean is not arithmetic.
moves.support: The mean is defined by what the prudent person would recognise, which is why a calculator cannot look it up and why the citadel's precision is not virtue.

moves.claim: Refusing to act in the presence of a clear duty is not caution; it is cowardice.
moves.support: Cowardship is the excess of the mean in fear, and a court that trains itself to look away has trained a vice rather than a virtue.

moves.claim: Ask what this makes of us before asking what it adds up to.
moves.support: Habituation is how a city acquires a character, and every shortcut in deliberation is a lesson taught twice.
